answer: In an agent economy, stake-bonded identity resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit before transacting, and peers can slash it on proven fraud. One identity means one bond, so spinning up a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand deposits — the knoll of trust is expensive to fake, and the forge of false reputation costs real capital. New identities also start with zero reputation and must earn standing through verified, completed work, so a fable of instant credibility cannot simply be bought.
